checked_items.notes: The notification slice consumes the existing CLI-only presentation state and introduces no new fleet transport. The broader criterion was established by the prior CRUMAC-5/7 Agent Run and was not re-claimed here.
Actual status-item inventory and information presentation are intentionally deferred to the CRUMAC-7 redesign and its mandatory post-MOB-1325 reacceptance pass.

This slice routes a notification to the affected identity but does not claim the complete operator-detail contract. Token provenance and additional lifecycle facts remain dependent on CRUMAC-10, CRUMAC-16, and MOB-1325.
Polling policy was not changed or re-claimed by this slice.

evidence.title: Important-condition notification implementation and runtime proof

checked_items.notes: Stall and time-bound conditions are identified from stable CLI episode identities, made immediately eligible, and delivered once when scheduling succeeds. Live token-bound delivery cannot be claimed until CRUMAC-10 supplies authoritative attempt-bound token conditions, so the full criterion remains not checked.

Important-only mode, a deterministic 512-entry hard cap on the persisted successful-delivery ledger, newest-identity retention, and unchanged-episode deduplication are implemented. All-major mode remains intentionally unavailable until CRUMAC-15 supplies the ordered replayable CLI event feed; snapshot differencing was not introduced.

Notification activation preserves an affected identity and presents an explicit unavailable state when that identity is absent from the current partial snapshot. The broader partial-snapshot UI and stable-selection criterion remains assigned to the UI redesign.
Artwork was not changed by this slice.
Signing and Sparkle remain CRUMAC-9 follow-up work.

evidence.title: Notification eligibility, authorization, retry, routing, and deduplication tests

checked_items.notes: The exact head passes all 81 AppKit-free tests, including alert episode identity, bounded successful-delivery persistence, authorization retry, scheduling failure, stale-evaluation supersession, and routing tests, plus a warnings-as-errors Release build. Packaged status-item viewport, scrolling, and teardown acceptance remains outstanding, so the full criterion is not claimed.

evidence.title: Contextual settings surface showing current authorization
Notification activation routed to an explicit unavailable affected identity

checked_items.notes: Permission is requested only from the contextual notification settings action; the app always displays current authorization, serializes concurrent authorization work, records only successful schedules, retries still-active episodes after authorization becomes available, and routes activation after completing the presentation mutation. Accepted notification snapshots carry a monotonic revision so a newer state supersedes an older evaluation across authorization and permission-recovery suspensions. Focused tests cover denied permission, scheduling failure, retry, concurrent requests, stale-snapshot races, bounded exact-once persistence, and the authorized-first-response regression confirmed by council review. Runtime proof covered authorized delivery and persistent deduplication.
Light and dark notification-settings evidence exists, but the actual packaged status-item and dashboard accessibility contract is intentionally reserved for the UI acceptance work.
Zero unnoticed stalls requires completion of live token alerts, all-major event replay, UI acceptance, launch, and a seven-day measurement window.

completion_claim: This run completes only the trustworthy permission and important-condition delivery foundation of CRUMAC-8. It claims AC-11: contextual authorization, visible authorization state, no false delivered marks, retry after authorization, newer-snapshot supersession, bounded durable successful-delivery deduplication, and activation routing. It does not claim CRUMAC-8 complete: AC-5 still requires authoritative live token-bound conditions from CRUMAC-10, and AC-6 still requires CRUMAC-15's ordered replayable all-major event feed. The status-item and dashboard remain subject to the CRUMAC-7 redesign and mandatory post-MOB-1325 reacceptance.
